speaker: Basil
before: "You fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's meant to be a fishing fee, but I've lost the receipt. Again. Please don't tell Chef."
after: "Um, you fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's meant to be a fishing fee, but I've lost the receipt again, so please don't tell Chef."

speaker: Basil
before: "Don't tell the taste testers you fainted. If anyone asks you anything, just say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."
after: "And don't tell the taste testers you fainted, either. If anyone asks you anything at all, just say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."

speaker: (narration)
before: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.
after: You've found a hidden stash that nobody has sampled or sauced, and it's all yours.

speaker: (narration)
before: Smooth, balanced, a touch of citrus. You nod like a professional. +HP.
after: It's smooth and balanced with a touch of citrus, and you nod like a professional. +HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: Your palate sharpens. You can taste what the cheese had for breakfast. A little extra HP for the visit.
after: Your palate sharpens until you can taste what the cheese had for breakfast. A little extra HP for the visit.

speaker: (narration)
before: You find the ghost pepper in spoon three. Your ears ring in protest. -1 HP.
after: You find the ghost pepper in spoon three, and your ears ring in protest. -1 HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: You ladle some soup. Tomato with a hint of basil. Warm all the way down. +HP.
after: You ladle up some soup: tomato with a hint of basil, and warm all the way down. +HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: Third ladle: minestrone, mostly noodles. You feel taller. +HP.
after: Your third ladle is minestrone, mostly noodles, and you feel taller for it. +HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.
after: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back, because you are full. The fountain takes it well.

speaker: (narration)
before: A lime gelatin sentinel with a spoon spear and a fruit cocktail soul. Prototype Mk. 2.
after: You face a lime gelatin sentinel with a spoon for a spear and a fruit cocktail for a soul: Prototype Mk. 2.

speaker: (narration)
before: You watch it wobble through a thought. Management has discouraged these.
after: You watch it wobble its way through a thought, which is something management has discouraged.

speaker: (narration)
before: A pot-bellied colonel with a lid for a hat and a ladle for a sword. Thirty years of service, forty years of cheese.
after: You face a pot-bellied colonel with a lid for a hat and a ladle for a sword, who has thirty years of service behind him and forty years of cheese.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: This deck is underdressed, darling. A little butter, a little foil, and voila.
after: Your deck is underdressed, my sweet. A little butter and a little foil, and voila.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Decorative cake, darling. Please admire it without cutlery.
after: The cake is decorative, my sweet, so please admire it without cutlery.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: A good answer is like a roux: patience, then butter. Mostly butter.
after: A good answer is like a roux: patience first, then butter, and an excellent finish.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Chalk again. Notes of limestone. Excellent body, no business being in my mouth.
after: Chalk again, with notes of limestone. Excellent body, and no business in my mouth.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: ORDER UP! Sixty seconds and a dream! WHOOSH! Mostly the dream!
after: ORDER UP! Welcome back to the show, sprouts! WHOOSH! You've been a lovely audience!

speaker: Basil
before: Chef ALWAYS tastes. Always. That's how you know it's Chef.
after: Um. Chef ALWAYS tastes, you see, always. That's how you know it's really Chef.

speaker: Basil
before: I'm brave. I'm brave. ...Have you seen my thyme? I'm running out of it.
after: I'm brave. I'm brave. ...Psst, have you eaten today? There's soup, if you'd like.

speaker: The Grand Chef (formerly Grand Chef Escoffina)
before: A full table is a safe table. Pull up a chair, dear - that's an order.
after: A full table is a safe table, so pull up a chair. That's an order, and so is seconds.

speaker: The Doppelganger (later named Escoffina)
before: I am a third-class apprentice now, with many dishes. I am trying. So are the dishes.
after: I am a third-class apprentice now. I wash many dishes. I broke one, and nobody shouted.

speaker: (narration)
before: A corrupted sous-chef guards the conveyor belt. Everything on the belt is a little too shiny.
after: A corrupted sous-chef stands guard over the conveyor belt, where everything is a little too shiny.

speaker: (narration)
before: A hot, honest meal: the only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.
after: Someone has kept one hot, honest meal going here, the only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: An experimental food construct, stitched together from three kinds of meat and one regret. (Elite)
after: You face an experimental food construct, stitched together from three kinds of meat and one regret. (Elite)

speaker: The Doppelganger, later Escoffina
before: The Grand Chef's private kitchen. Her apron is spotless, and something about her chin is a little off.
after: You've reached the Grand Chef's private kitchen, where her apron is spotless and something about her chin is a little off.
